Whether used on its own or as part of a fantasy asset pack, this Amanita mushroom is a must-have for adding color, playfulness, and natural magic to your digital forest world.

description_text:
Eilean Donan (Scottish Gaelic: Eilean Donnain) is a small tidal island where three sea lochs meet, Loch Duich, Loch Long and Loch Alsh, in the western Highlands of Scotland. A picturesque castle that frequently appears in photographs, film and television dominates the island, which lies about 1 kilometre (5⁄8 mi) from the village of Dornie. Since the castle’s restoration in the early 20th century, a footbridge has connected the island to the mainland.
Eilean Donan is part of the Kintail National Scenic Area, one of 40 in Scotland.[2] In 2001, the island had a recorded population of just one person,[3] but there were no “usual residents” at the time of the 2011 census.[1]
The castle was founded in the thirteenth century, and became a stronghold of the Clan Mackenzie and their allies the Clan MacRae. In the early eighteenth century, the Mackenzies’ involvement in the Jacobite rebellions led in 1719 to the castle’s destruction by government ships (Wikipedia)

The Old Abandoned Rusty Cars pack is a high-detail post-apocalyptic vehicle collection designed for cinematic environments, games, and photorealistic renders. This set captures the visual narrative of long-term abandonment, natural overgrowth, and structural decay.
Design & Style
The overall design follows a post-apocalyptic, urban decay aesthetic, blending mechanical deterioration with organic invasion. The vehicles appear untouched for decades, overtaken by nature and environmental exposure. The style emphasizes realism, surface storytelling, and environmental integration, making it ideal for survival scenes, ruined cities, forest takeovers, and dystopian landscapes.
The forms remain faithful to realistic automotive proportions:

  - The compact car features a rounded, collapsed silhouette with dented panels and corroded surfaces.

  - The cargo van maintains a boxy industrial shape, partially intact but heavily rust-stained and overgrown.

  - The motorcycle frame is skeletal and stripped down, exposing structural geometry.

  - The detached seat and engine block add modular storytelling elements for scene dressing.

Materials

  - All assets are built with physically based rendering (PBR) materials, focusing on layered surface degradation:

  - Oxidized steel with advanced rust variation (dark brown, orange corrosion, flaking metal)

  - Peeling automotive paint with edge wear and exposed primer

  - Dirty glass with grime and opacity variation

  - Rubber components with desaturation and aging

  - Organic foliage materials with leaf translucency and natural color variation

  - Soil and dust accumulation in crevices and lower body sections

Vegetation is integrated directly into the vehicles, with vines wrapping around mirrors, windows, grilles, and interiors. Leaves penetrate broken glass areas and open cavities, reinforcing the sense of time and abandonment.
Colors
The pack features a natural, earthy palette:

  - Deep rust browns

The image is a comprehensive, bright, and creatives stylized low-poly 3D render, bringing together all the distinct building and tree models from the previous individual images into a single, cohesive urban landscape. The scene is set on a much larger, continuous green grassy field with an interconnected network of grey asphalt roads and sidewalks that link the structures and create a functional-looking city block. The specific pedestrian crosswalk is visible on one of the main streets.
Two main multi-story buildings serve as architectural anchors:
On the left, the tall, distinct white building with horizontal brown stripes and large windows is positioned near a junction, as seen in image_9.png.
On the right, the complex, multi-colored (turquoise, orange, blue glass panels) modern residential or office tower is featured, showcasing the detail from image_10.png and image_11.png.

Prominently featured in the light blue sky above the entire scene are two stylized 3D low-poly text elements:
The main title is Low Poly Urban Environment in large, faceted, multi-colored letters.
Below it, a smaller text reads Free Download in orange, faceted letters.
The lighting is bright and warm, casting distinct geometric shadows and highlighting the faceted textures of all objects. Small, added low-poly details like benches, a bus stop sign, and a small park area with a low-poly fountain are included to enhance the creative feel. The entire scene has a playful, miniature world atmosphere.

description_text:
Dianthus gratianopolitanus Grass 01
Dianthus gratianopolitanus, commonly known as the Cheddar pink or clove pink, is a species of plant in the family Caryophyllaceae. It is a herbaceous perennial, hardy to zones 4–8. It grows to a height of 0.5 to 1 feet, blooming from May to June. Flowers are fragrant and rose pink. Grows best in full sun and has medium water requirements. Overwatering or poor drainage leads to crown rot, and plants do not tolerate wet winter soil conditions. The specific epithet gratianopolitanus refers to the ancient Roman name Gratianopolis of the modern French city of Grenoble. The common name Cheddar pink refers to the fact that it's native to the Cheddar Gorge in England. It is native to western and central Europe, from the UK to Ukraine. It became a protected species in the UK in 1975 under the Conservation of Wild Creatures and Wild Plants Act.

  - 2x Albedo/Diffuse (4K)

  - File names (textures & meshes) are simple to understand;

  - Easy modification;

  - Low-mid polycount;

  - Royalty-free licence and free price.

If you have any questions/suggestions, please, write that in a comment section or contact me on my e-mail: andriyandriy1956@outlook.com
Thank you!

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia:The Utah teapot, or the Newell teapot, is a 3D test model that has become a standard reference object and an in-joke within the computer graphics community. It is a mathematical model of an ordinary Melitta-brand teapot that appears solid with a nearly rotationally symmetrical body. Using a teapot model is considered the 3D equivalent of a Hello, World! program, a way to create an easy 3D scene with a somewhat complex model acting as the basic geometry for a scene with a light setup. Some programming libraries, such as the OpenGL Utility Toolkit, even have functions dedicated to drawing teapots.
The teapot model was created in 1975 by early computer graphics researcher Martin Newell, a member of the pioneering graphics program at the University of Utah. It was one of the first to be modeled (using bézier curves) rather than precisely measured.

title: simple versatile flowerpot Free 3D print model

total_file_size: 3MF:252 KB
description_text:
hello to all! this is one of my first designs with mastercam. its meant to be a flowerpot. however, with some simple scaling in your favorite 3d slicer, teacups, cups, bowls, anything that can hold liquid can be made! if you wanted to use this as a flowerpot id advise using this for smaller plants, as i only have about 20-30% infill on mine, and drilling holes in anything that isnt 100% filled may be met with unwanted bacteria/ wildlife living inside of the design (and 20% infill may use up a full spool, probably like 60% of it, so for infill do about 10%, unless you want a solid pot, then 20% is more than strong enough ). it is a relatively large at 6.5375 in. diameter on top, and a very slightly larger base at 6.75 in. Inside is 5 in. tall. this tool me 14 hours to print. i recommend 230 Celsius and .1 layer thickness, as itll help to have a cleaner look. it also has a small draft, making it slightly larger up top. 
The best material to use for this would be ABS, as it is the most proper material that will not collect any bacteria & is 100% safe for indoor & outdoor uses. If made with PLA it should really only be considered novelty. Abs is the proper material!! 
THIS IS AN ORIGINAL DESIGN BY ME! -Emanuel Lopez

The cactus was created on blender using geometry nodes. It is therefore recommended to use it on blender. There are also other formats in the zipper file, but they will not be optimized.
Mostly used as ornamental plants, but some are also crop plants, they are unusual and easily identifiable plants that have managed to adapt to extremely arid and hot environments by developing various physiological and anatomical features to conserve water. Their stems have adapted by becoming succulent and photosynthetic, while their leaves, very often, have become spines, one of the most distinctive features of plants in this family.
Cacti come in very different shapes and sizes, from small and globular to large and columnar. The tallest cactus is Pachycereus pringlei, with a maximum recorded height of 19.2 m[3], and the smallest is Blossfeldia liliputana, which reaches 1 cm in diameter when fully mature[4]. Cactus flowers are large compared to the stem and leaves, and just like spines and branches, they arise from areoles. Many cactus species have night blooms because they are pollinated by nocturnal insects or small nocturnal animals.

Middle Hole Ice Cube 3D Model DescriptionTitle: Realistic Middle Hole Ice Cube 3D Model
Bring a unique and refreshing element to your projects with this highly detailed middle hole ice cube 3D model. Ideal for advertising, product visualization, food and beverage renders, and more, this model adds a distinctive touch with its realistic design and attention to detail.
Features:
  - 
Realistic Design: This middle hole ice cube model is crafted with precision, featuring a central hole that adds an interesting visual element. The cube's edges are slightly rounded, and the surface includes subtle cracks, bubbles, and frosty textures for enhanced realism.

  - 
High-Resolution Textures: Equipped with high-resolution textures that accurately capture the intricate details of ice, including its translucency and light refractions, providing a lifelike appearance.

  - 
Advanced Materials and Shaders: Includes physically-based rendering (PBR) materials and shaders to replicate the properties of real ice, with accurate reflection, refraction, and subsurface scattering for a realistic effect.

  - 
Optimized Geometry: The model is optimized for performance, ensuring it integrates smoothly into your projects without sacrificing detail. The polygon count is balanced to offer high-quality visuals while maintaining efficiency.

  - 
Multiple File Formats: Available in various file formats, including .obj, .fbx, .stl, and .blend, making it compatible with major 3D software such as Blender, 3ds Max, Maya, and Cinema 4D.

  - 
Customizable: Fully UV-mapped, allowing easy customization and application of additional textures or effects if needed.

Applications:
  - 
Advertising: Perfect for creating eye-catching visuals for beverage and food advertisements, emphasizing the refreshing and unique quality of drinks.

  - 
Product Visualization: Enhance product renders, particularly those related to beverages, kitchenware, and summer-themed products, with a distinctive touch.

  - 
Food and Beverage Renders: Ideal for scenes involving cocktails, soft drinks, or any chilled beverages, adding a realistic and unique touch to your culinary 3D renders.

  - 
Game Development: Suitable for use in game environments where realistic ice elements are needed, especially in scenes involving bars, restaurants, or cold settings.

Minimalist Elephant – 3D Printable SculptureThis is a clean, modern elephant sculpture designed with minimalism and organic elegance in mind.Perfect for interior decoration, artistic collections, or for any 3D printing enthusiast who appreciates stylish, fluid forms.
InspirationI was inspired after seeing a similar elephant model being sold as a plant pot holder — but it was far too expensive.That pushed me back to the “drawing board” to create my own minimalist version, and honestly... I think it turned out pretty decent. :D
Print InformationThis model was printed using ABS Marble from Voolt3D on a Creality K1 with Unicorn all-metal hotend.
Print Settings:
Layer height: 0.20 mm
Nozzle: 245 °C
Bed: 100 °C
Fan: OFF (as recommended for ABS)
Speed: ~60 mm/s
Adhesion: Brim enabled
The marble texture gave the model an elegant and subtle stone-like finish.
Recommended Scale80–120 mm in height, depending on your intended use (decor, gift, display piece).
Other Suggested MaterialsPLA
Silk PLA
PETG
Resin
This model is perfect for FDM and resin printers, and very friendly for beginners.
Support NotesSupports were manually enabled under the feet gaps and beneath the trunk to improve bed adhesion and prevent fragile overhangs from breaking before merging with the body.They were easy to remove and did not compromise the final look.

I created a 3d isometric stylish bedroom in blender by following this tutorial for the model and scene layout. 
https://youtu.be/Bzy6TMxVOmg?si=lb2Poracphtjjr1w
Twenty Shades of Gray
The concept behind this project is built around exploring the versatility of grey tones in interior design. By layering dark, medium, light, and metallic greys, I created contrast, depth, and harmony without relying on bright colors. Each shade was carefully assigned to specific materials, from fabrics and woods to metals and stone, to highlight how subtle variations of grey can define mood, texture, and style in a space. The result is a cohesive and modern isometric bedroom that feels sophisticated yet balanced, all unified under a monochromatic motif.
Modifications:
- Added a model of a mouse(kinda messed up in the process but it's still in shape) and mousepad    - Changed the bedside coffee table in an interesting shape    - Added a plant pot and moved the porcelain jar to the bedside drawer    - Added a copy of a model of an open book on the small table model    - Textured curtains    - Added a model of curtain rods
Textures
All textures are originally picked from blenderkit/made by myself. If you want to use textures of ellmodel, buy the model with the textures from her patreon (link in her yt).
Here is the list of all the textures I used:
Dark Grays / Near Black:
Black Olive – Bed frame |            Nero Marquina – Floor |             Dark Charcoal – Coffee Table |            Anthracit Ceramic – Computer Table |            Anthracit Titanit – Bedside Drawers |            Linen Upholstery Dark Grey – (sofa/bed element) |            Dark Gray Fabric – Sofa / Medium pillow |            Slate Gray - Curtains 
Medium Grays:
Spanish Gray – Ceiling (Procedural) |            Gray Wood Veneer – Chair |            Gray Ash Wood Veneer – Plant pot table |            Plain Grey Suede – Blanket / Small pillows |            Leaves Grey Chenille – Sofa pillow 1 |            Stripe Grey Sheer – Sofa pillow 2 |            Davy’s Grey – Cup 
Light Grays:
Porcelain – Vase / Plant pot |            Chinese White – Mirror (Procedural)
Metallic Grays: 
Sonic Silver – Lamp (Procedural) |            Brushed Aluminum – Monitor  |            Brushed Satin Nickel – Drawer handles
Notify me if no textures are present in the model. A like before downloading is highly appreciated :)

Concept
I made this project about 4 years ago on February 2022 for pawnisher's infinite journey contest. the project is my first experience with non-destructive modeling and semi-procedural texturing. now the project was not finished in time and i did only the modeling and later on texturing and i have been busy since but finally a week ago i decided to finish it to share it with you, i made a quick setup for the lighting and added a character from daz, made her a hoodie and rendered the final images.
The concept of this render comes from the contest, endless journey, a very long journey inside a spaceship, such journey can become very boring as there is not much to look at, except stars. ( i know they are beautiful but looking at the same scene for years... ) so the idea was that the character enters the room with zero gravity, grabs on to the red handle, activates the gravity from the panel mounted to the wall, takes of her shoes, sits by the window, grabs her tablet, plays a music and then chooses a scenery which will take place on the window, the window turns into a display, displaying whatever is the theme of the song or the character wants to see. a train ride through a rainy forest, a train ride with cityscape view in lo-fi style, or skyscrapers with neon lights and glowing windows under water like bioshock perhaps and so on.though, I didn't have time to finish the project, in fact i only rendered it 3-4 years later. so I'm sharing it with you for free.

description_text:
The object in the images is a traditional Kerala “Uruli.” 
A uruli is a wide, shallow bowl traditionally made of brass or bronze and commonly used in South India, especially in Kerala. In the past, it was mainly used for cooking large quantities of food, such as payasam (a sweet dessert) during temple festivals and big family gatherings. Because the metal distributes heat evenly, it was perfect for slow cooking.
Today, urulis are also widely used as decorative elements. People fill them with water, floating flowers, candles, or lotus petals and place them at entrances, wedding stages, hotels, and homes to create a traditional and welcoming ambiance. The design you shared has lotus-petal carvings around the side, which is a common Indian decorative motif symbolizing purity and prosperity.

description_text: A bushing or rubber bushing is a type of vibration isolator. It provides an interface between two parts, damping the energy transmitted through the bushing. A common application is in vehicle suspension systems, where a bushing made of rubber (or, more often, synthetic rubber or polyurethane) separates the faces of two metal objects while allowing a certain amount of movement. This movement allows the suspension parts to move freely, for example, when traveling over a large bump, while minimizing transmission of noise and small vibrations through to the chassis of the vehicle. A rubber bushing may also be described as a flexible mounting or antivibration mounting.

The dominant species in the Mulga, which is Acacia aneura, is called True Mulga. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Mulga is the Indigenous Australian name for the semi-arid scrub that covers a large part of Australian mainland. The dominant species in the Mulga, which is Acacia aneura, is called True Mulga. True Mulga is a very variable species, that can be found as low shrub or medium sized tree, depending on the growing conditions. It is long lived (200 to 300 years) when undisturbed by fire. It can collect rainfall through the phyllodes and it’s roots can reach deep waters. Differently from Eucalypt Woodland, Mulga has a very limited capability to re-sprout after fire. True Mulga is a valuable fodder source for Australia’s pastoral industry. Origin : Central and Western Australia. Height : up to 15 m., commonly 7 m.

I'll update the model as new photographs of the lectern become available.
Please, enjoy the model and rate/review accordingly.

The dominant species in the Mulga, which is Acacia aneura, is called True Mulga. True Mulga is a very variable species, that can be found as low shrub or medium sized tree, depending on the growing conditions. It is long lived (200 to 300 years) when undisturbed by fire. It can collect rainfall through the phyllodes and it’s roots can reach deep waters. Differently from Eucalypt Woodland, Mulga has a very limited capability to re-sprout after fire. description_text:
Plummer block or Pedestal bearing is used for long shafts, requiring intermediate support, especially when the shaft
cannot be introduced in the bearing end-wise. It consists of a pedestal or base, a cap and a
bush, split into two halves, called ‘bearing brasses’. The split parts used in the assembly, facilitate
easy assembly and periodical replacement of the worn-out brasses.
After placing the journal on the lower half of the bush, kept in the base, the upper half
of the bush is placed and the cap is then fixed to the pedestal, by means of two bolts.
Flanges are provided at either end of the bush, to prevent its axial motion. The rotary motion
of the bush is prevented by a snug provided at the bottom of the lower brass, fitting into a
corresponding hole in the base.

description_text:
A fern is a member of a group of vascular plants (plants with xylem and phloem) that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers. They differ from mosses by being vascular, i.e., having specialized tissues that conduct water and nutrients, in having branched stems and in having life cycles in which the sporophyte is the dominant phase. Like other vascular plants, ferns have complex leaves called megaphylls, that are more complex than the microphylls of clubmosses. description_text:
The dog (Canis familiaris when considered a distinct species or Canis lupus familiaris when considered a subspecies of the wolf)[5] is a domesticated carnivore of the family Canidae. It is part of the wolf-like canids,[6] and is the most widely abundant terrestrial carnivore.[7][8][9][10][11] The dog and the extant gray wolf are sister taxa[12][13][14] as modern wolves are not closely related to the wolves that were first domesticated,[13][14] which implies that the direct ancestor of the dog is extinct.[15] The dog was the first species to be domesticated,[14][16] and has been selectively bred over millennia for various behaviors, sensory capabilities, and physical attributes.[17]
Their long association with humans has led dogs to be uniquely attuned to human behavior[18] and they are able to thrive on a starch-rich diet that would be inadequate for other canids.[19] Dogs vary widely in shape, size and colors.[20] They perform many roles for humans, such as hunting, herding, pulling loads, protection, assisting police and military, companionship and, more recently, aiding disabled people and therapeutic roles. This influence on human society has given them the sobriquet of man's best friend.

description_text: Elephants are the largest existing land animals. Three living species are currently recognised: the African bush elephant, the African forest elephant, and the Asian elephant. They are the only surviving members of the family Elephantidae and the order Proboscidea. The order was formerly much more diverse during the Pleistocene, but most species became extinct during the Late Pleistocene epoch. Distinctive features of elephants include a long proboscis called a trunk, tusks, large ear flaps, pillar-like legs, and tough but sensitive skin. The trunk is used for breathing, bringing food and water to the mouth, and grasping objects. Tusks, which are derived from the incisor teeth, serve both as weapons and as tools for moving objects and digging. The large ear flaps assist in maintaining a constant body temperature as well as in communication. African elephants have larger ears and concave backs, whereas Asian elephants have smaller ears, and convex or level backs.

The models follow a semi-stylized visual approach, blending naturalistic wood detail with exaggerated, smooth snow formations. The style fits winter forests, magical landscapes, stylized open-world games, and fantasy cinematics. The hand-crafted shapes emphasize character and mood, with some trees leaning, twisting, or forming expressive root structures.

Each tree is designed to stand as an individual hero prop or blend into a winter environment when used as part of a forest set.
